changes: Copy only the upstream xargs module; omit unrelated find/locate dependencies.

Original WASI adapter executes explicit argv with the existing waffle-process-consumer; native execution uses upstream std::process for controlled tests only. Runtime cwd initializes libc, environment and inherited descriptors are preserved; stdin input supplies child EOF via an owned closed-writer pipe, while -a retains stdin.

GNU child outcome mapping distinguishes exits, signals and startup failures; shared consumer owns cancellation, caller-fatal jobs and physical-retirement wait. No process state machine or protocol is copied.
Preserve empty byte-delimited input items; upstream discarded consecutive delimiters. Readers and batching otherwise remain upstream, including their UTF-8 input contract.

Reject parallelism and replacement before input access. Default no-command echo is print-only; help states unsupported modes. The byte-delimited reader unit test now expects GNU-compatible empty items; historical Bash fixtures and oracle observations are unchanged.
